120.00.plain: Assault in the third degree covers intentionally or recklessly causing physical injury, or causing it with criminal negligence by a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: he causes such injury to such person or to a third person
causes physical injury to another person

120.01.plain: Reckless assault of a child by a child day care provider covers recklessly causing serious physical injury to a child under eleven in the provider's care; it is a class E felony.
acts: causes serious physical injury to a child under the care of such provider or employee who is less than eleven years of age

120.02.plain: Reckless assault of a child covers an adult recklessly causing serious injury to the brain of a child under five by shaking or by slamming or throwing the child; it is a class D felony.
acts: causes serious physical injury to the brain of a child less than five years old by shaking the child, or by slamming or throwing the child so as to impact the child's head on a hard surface or object

120.03.plain: Vehicular assault in the second degree covers causing serious physical injury while operating a motor vehicle, vessel, snowmobile or all terrain vehicle in violation of listed intoxication or impairment laws; it is a class E felony.
acts: causes serious physical injury to another person
operates a motor vehicle in violation of subdivision two, three, four or four-a of section eleven hundred ninety-two of the vehicle and traffic law
operates a motor vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of more than eighteen thousand pounds which contains flammable gas, radioactive materials or explosives
operates a snowmobile in violation of paragraph (b), (c) or (d) of subdivision one of section 25.24 of the parks, recreation and historic preservation law

120.04.plain: Vehicular assault in the first degree covers committing vehicular assault in the second degree with an aggravating factor such as .18 blood alcohol, a suspended license, a prior conviction, multiple victims or a child passenger; it is a class D felony.
acts: commits the crime of vehicular assault in the second degree as defined in section 120.03 of this article

120.04-A.plain: Aggravated vehicular assault covers reckless driving plus vehicular assault in the second degree, with an aggravating factor such as .18 blood alcohol, a suspended license, a prior conviction, multiple victims or a child passenger; it is a class C felony.
acts: engages in reckless driving as defined by section twelve hundred twelve of the vehicle and traffic law
commits the crime of vehicular assault in the second degree as defined in section 120.03 of this article

120.05.plain: Assault in the second degree covers many listed assaults, including intentionally causing serious injury, injury with a weapon, injury to protected workers, children and the elderly; it is a class D felony.
acts: he causes such injury to such person or to a third person
causes physical injury to such employee
causes serious physical injury to another person by means of a deadly weapon or a dangerous instrument
causes physical injury to another person who is a child under the age of eighteen by intentional discharge of a firearm, rifle or shotgun
causes stupor, unconsciousness or other physical impairment or injury to another person by administering to him, without his consent, a drug, substance or preparation capable of producing the same
causes physical injury to a person other than one of the participants
causes serious physical injury to such person
causes such injury to an employee of a school or public school district
causes physical injury to such process server

120.06.plain: Gang assault in the second degree covers causing serious physical injury with intent to cause physical injury while aided by two or more other persons present; it is a class C felony.
acts: he causes serious physical injury to such person or to a third person

120.07.plain: Gang assault in the first degree covers causing serious physical injury with intent to cause serious physical injury while aided by two or more other persons present; it is a class B felony.
acts: he causes serious physical injury to such person or to a third person

120.08.plain: Assault on a peace officer, police officer, firefighter or emergency medical services professional covers causing serious physical injury to prevent the lawful duty; it is a class C felony.
acts: causes serious physical injury to such peace officer, police officer, firefighter, paramedic or technician

120.09.plain: Assault on a judge covers causing serious physical injury to a judge with intent to prevent official judicial duties; it is a class C felony.
acts: causes serious physical injury to such judge

120.09-A.plain: Aggravated assault on a judge covers causing serious physical injury to a judge with intent to cause serious injury and prevent official judicial duties; it is a class B felony.
acts: causes serious physical injury to such judge

120.10.plain: Assault in the first degree covers intentionally causing serious injury with a weapon, intentional disfigurement or disabling, depraved-indifference recklessness, and injury during a felony; it is a class B felony.
acts: he causes such injury to such person or to a third person by means of a deadly weapon or a dangerous instrument
he causes such injury to such person or to a third person
engages in conduct which creates a grave risk of death to another person, and thereby causes serious physical injury to another person
causes serious physical injury to a person other than one of the participants

120.11.plain: Aggravated assault upon a police officer or a peace officer covers intentionally causing serious injury to one by deadly weapon or dangerous instrument; it is a class B felony.
acts: he causes such injury by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument

120.12.plain: Aggravated assault upon a person less than eleven years old covers an adult committing third degree assault on such a child after a prior conviction within ten years; it is a class E felony.
acts: commits the crime of assault in the third degree as defined in section 120.00 of this article upon a person less than eleven years old

120.13.plain: Menacing in the first degree covers committing menacing in the second degree after a prior conviction for it or for menacing a police officer or peace officer within ten years; it is a class E felony.
acts: commits the crime of menacing in the second degree

120.14.plain: Menacing in the second degree covers placing another in fear of injury or death by displaying a weapon, stalking-like repeated conduct, or menacing in violation of an order of protection; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: places or attempts to place another person in reasonable fear of physical injury, serious physical injury or death by displaying a deadly weapon
repeatedly follows a person or engages in a course of conduct or repeatedly commits acts over a period of time
commits the crime of menacing in the third degree in violation of that part of a duly served order of protection

120.15.plain: Menacing in the third degree covers intentionally placing or attempting to place another in fear of death or injury by physical menace; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: places or attempts to place another person in fear of death, imminent serious physical injury or physical injury

120.16.plain: Hazing in the first degree covers intentionally or recklessly engaging in conduct in the course of initiation or affiliation that creates a substantial risk of physical injury and thereby causes injury; it is a class a misdemeanor.
acts: engages in conduct, including, but not limited to, making physical contact with or requiring physical activity of such other person, which creates a substantial risk of physical injury to such other person or a third person and thereby causes such injury

120.17.plain: Hazing in the second degree covers intentionally or recklessly engaging in conduct in the course of initiation or affiliation that creates a substantial risk of physical injury; it is a violation.
acts: engages in conduct, including, but not limited to, making physical contact with or requiring physical activity of such other person, which creates a substantial risk of physical injury to such other person or a third person

120.18.plain: Menacing a police officer or peace officer covers intentionally placing one in fear of injury or death by displaying a weapon; it is a class D felony.
acts: places or attempts to place a police officer or peace officer in reasonable fear of physical injury, serious physical injury or death by displaying a deadly weapon, knife, pistol, revolver, rifle, shotgun, machine gun or other firearm, whether operable or not

120.19.plain: Assault on a retail worker covers causing physical injury to a retail worker to prevent an act within the scope of employment; it is a class E felony.
acts: causes physical injury to such retail worker

120.20.plain: Reckless endangerment in the second degree covers recklessly creating a substantial risk of serious physical injury to another; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: engages in conduct which creates a substantial risk of serious physical injury to another person

120.25.plain: Reckless endangerment in the first degree covers recklessly creating a grave risk of death to another under circumstances showing depraved indifference; it is a class D felony.
acts: engages in conduct which creates a grave risk of death to another person

120.30.plain: Promoting a suicide attempt covers intentionally causing or aiding another person to attempt suicide; it is a class E felony.
acts: causes or aids another person to attempt suicide

120.35.plain: Provides that a person whose conduct is both promoting a suicide attempt and attempt to commit murder may not be convicted of attempt to commit murder unless he causes or aids the suicide attempt by duress or deception.

120.40.plain: Defines terms used in the stalking sections of this article.

120.45.plain: Stalking in the fourth degree covers intentionally engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person, with no legitimate purpose, that causes or is likely to cause fear or harm; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: engages in a course of conduct directed at a specific person

120.50.plain: Stalking in the third degree covers repeated fourth degree stalking against several persons or after prior convictions, or intentionally engaging in a course of conduct likely to cause fear of injury; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: Commits the crime of stalking in the fourth degree in violation of section 120.45 of this article
engages in a course of conduct directed at such person

120.55.plain: Stalking in the second degree covers aggravated third degree stalking, such as displaying a weapon, prior convictions, stalking a child under fourteen, or stalking ten or more persons; it is a class E felony.
acts: Commits the crime of stalking in the third degree as defined in subdivision three of section 120.50 of this article
repeatedly follows a person under the age of fourteen or engages in a course of conduct or repeatedly commits acts over a period of time

120.60.plain: Stalking in the first degree is committing stalking in the third or second degree and, in the course and furtherance, causing physical injury or committing a listed sex offense; it is a class D felony.
acts: commits the crime of stalking in the third degree as defined in subdivision three of section 120.50 or stalking in the second degree as defined in section 120.55 of this article
causes physical injury to the victim of such crime

commits a class A misdemeanor defined in article one hundred thirty of this chapter, or a class E felony defined in section 130.25, former section 130.40 or section 130.85 of this chapter, or a class D felony defined in former section 130.45 or section 130.30 of this chapter

120.70.plain: Luring a child is luring a child under seventeen into a vehicle, aircraft, watercraft, isolated area or building to commit a listed offense against the child; class E felony, raised to class C or D if the intended offense was a class A or B felony.
acts: lures a child into a motor vehicle, aircraft, watercraft, isolated area, building, or part thereof

121.11.plain: Criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation is pressing on the throat or neck, or blocking the nose or mouth, of another with intent to impede breathing or blood circulation; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: applies pressure on the throat or neck of such person
blocks the nose or mouth of such person

121.12.plain: Strangulation in the second degree is criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation that causes stupor, loss of consciousness, or other physical injury or impairment; it is a class D felony.
acts: commits the crime of criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation, as defined in section 121.11 of this article, and thereby causes stupor, loss of consciousness for any period of time, or any other physical injury or impairment

121.13.plain: Strangulation in the first degree is criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation that causes serious physical injury to the other person; it is a class C felony.
acts: commits the crime of criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation, as defined in section 121.11 of this article, and thereby causes serious physical injury to such other person

121.13-A.plain: Aggravated strangulation is a police or peace officer committing criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation, or using a chokehold or similar restraint, and thereby causing serious physical injury or death; it is a class C felony.
acts: commits the crime of criminal obstruction of breathing or blood circulation, as defined in section 121.11 of this article

uses a chokehold or similar restraint, as described in paragraph b of subdivision one of section eight hundred thirty-seven-t of the executive law, and thereby causes serious physical injury or death to another person

121.14.plain: Makes it an affirmative defense to sections 121.11, 121.12, 121.13 and 121.13-a that the conduct was for a valid medical or dental purpose.

125.00.plain: Defines homicide as conduct which causes the death of a person under circumstances constituting murder, manslaughter in the first or second degree, or criminally negligent homicide.

125.05.plain: Defines "person," when referring to the victim of a homicide, as a human being who has been born and is alive.

125.10.plain: Criminally negligent homicide is causing the death of another person with criminal negligence; it is a class E felony.
acts: causes the death of another person

125.11.plain: Aggravated criminally negligent homicide is causing, with criminal negligence, the death of a police or peace officer performing official duties; it is a class C felony.
acts: causes the death of a police officer or peace officer

125.12.plain: Vehicular manslaughter in the second degree is causing a death while operating a motor vehicle, vessel, snowmobile or all terrain vehicle in violation of listed intoxication or impairment laws; it is a class D felony.
acts: causes the death of another person
operates a motor vehicle in violation of subdivision two, three, four or four-a of section eleven hundred ninety-two of the vehicle and traffic law
operates a vessel or public vessel in violation of paragraph (b), (c), (d) or (e) of subdivision two of section forty-nine-a of the navigation law

operates a motor vehicle with a gross vehicle weight rating of more than eighteen thousand pounds which contains flammable gas, radioactive materials or explosives in violation of subdivision one of section eleven hundred ninety-two of the vehicle and traffic law
operates a snowmobile in violation of paragraph (b), (c) or (d) of subdivision one of section 25.24 of the parks, recreation and historic preservation law

operates an all terrain vehicle as defined in paragraph (a) of subdivision one of section twenty-two hundred eighty-one of the vehicle and traffic law in violation of subdivision two, three, four, or four-a of section eleven hundred ninety-two of the vehicle and traffic law

125.13.plain: Vehicular manslaughter in the first degree is committing vehicular manslaughter in the second degree with an aggravating factor such as .18 blood alcohol, suspended license, prior conviction, multiple deaths or a child passenger; it is a class C felony.
acts: commits the crime of vehicular manslaughter in the second degree as defined in section 125.12 of this article

commits such crime while operating a motor vehicle while such person has .18 of one per centum or more by weight of alcohol in such person's blood as shown by chemical analysis of such person's blood, breath, urine or saliva made pursuant to the provisions of section eleven hundred ninety-four of the vehicle and traffic law
causes the death of more than one other person
commits such crime while operating a motor vehicle while a child who is fifteen years of age or less is a passenger in such motor vehicle and causes the death of such child

commits such crime while operating a vessel in violation of paragraph (e-1) of subdivision two of section forty-nine-a of the navigation law while a child who is fifteen years of age or less is a passenger in such vessel and causes the death of such child

125.14.plain: Aggravated vehicular homicide is reckless driving plus vehicular manslaughter in the second degree with an aggravating factor such as .18 blood alcohol, suspended license, prior conviction or multiple victims; it is a class B felony.
acts: engages in reckless driving as defined by section twelve hundred twelve of the vehicle and traffic law
commits the crime of vehicular manslaughter in the second degree as defined in section 125.12 of this article
causes the death of more than one other person
causes the death of one person and the serious physical injury of at least one other person

125.15.plain: Manslaughter in the second degree is recklessly causing the death of another person, or intentionally causing or aiding another person to commit suicide; it is a class C felony.
acts: causes the death of another person
causes or aids another person to commit suicide

125.20.plain: Manslaughter in the first degree covers causing death with intent to cause serious injury, killing under extreme emotional disturbance, and recklessly causing the death of a child under eleven; it is a class B felony.
acts: causes the death of such person or of a third person
engages in conduct which creates a grave risk of serious physical injury to such person and thereby causes the death of such person

125.21.plain: Aggravated manslaughter in the second degree is recklessly causing the death of a police or peace officer performing official duties; it is a class C felony.
acts: causes the death of a police officer or peace officer

125.22.plain: Aggravated manslaughter in the first degree is killing a police or peace officer performing official duties with intent to cause serious injury, or with intent to kill under extreme emotional disturbance; it is a class B felony.
acts: causes the death of such officer or another police officer or peace officer

125.25.plain: Murder in the second degree covers intentional killing, depraved-indifference killing, felony murder, and killings of children under eleven or during listed sex crimes against children under fourteen; it is a class A-I felony.
acts: causes the death of such person or of a third person
engages in conduct which creates a grave risk of death to another person, and thereby causes the death of another person

commits or attempts to commit robbery, burglary, kidnapping, arson, rape in the first degree, a crime formerly defined in section 130.50 of this title, the crime of sexual abuse in the first degree, aggravated sexual abuse, escape in the first degree, or escape in the second degree
causes the death of a person other than one of the participants
engages in conduct which creates a grave risk of serious physical injury or death to another person less than eleven years old and thereby causes the death of such person
causes the death of such person

125.26.plain: Aggravated murder is intentionally killing a police officer, peace officer, first responder or correctional employee on duty, or intentionally killing a child under fourteen by torture, by a defendant over eighteen; it is a class A-I felony.
acts: causes the death of such person, or of a third person who was a person described in subparagraph (i), (ii), (ii-a) or (iii) of paragraph (a) of this subdivision engaged at the time of the killing in the course of performing his or her official duties
causes the death of such person

125.27.plain: Murder in the first degree is intentionally killing, by a defendant over eighteen, where a listed aggravating circumstance applies, such as the victim being a police officer, a contract killing or multiple victims; it is a class A-I felony.
acts: causes the death of such person or of a third person

130.00.plain: Defines terms used in Article 130, such as vaginal, oral and anal sexual contact, sexual contact, forcible compulsion, mentally disabled, and physically helpless.

130.05.plain: Makes lack of consent an element of every offense in this article and sets out when lack of consent results and who is deemed incapable of consent.

130.10.plain: Sets affirmative defenses and limits for prosecutions under Article 130, including lack of knowledge of incapacity, medical purpose, patient consent after advice, and marriage.

130.16.plain: Bars conviction under this article, where lack of consent rests solely on mental defect or incapacity, on the victim's testimony alone without supporting evidence.

130.20.plain: Sexual misconduct is vaginal, oral or anal sexual contact with another person without consent, or sexual conduct with an animal or a dead human body; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: engages in vaginal sexual contact with another person
engages in oral sexual contact with another person
engages in anal sexual contact with another person
engages in sexual conduct with an animal or a dead human body

130.25.plain: Rape in the third degree is vaginal, oral or anal sexual contact with a person incapable of consent for reasons other than age, with a person under seventeen by an actor twenty-one or older, or without consent; it is a class E felony.
acts: engages in vaginal sexual contact with another person
engages in oral sexual contact with another person
engages in anal sexual contact with another person

130.30.plain: Rape in the second degree is vaginal, oral or anal sexual contact by an actor eighteen or older with a person under fifteen, or with a person incapable of consent by mental disability or incapacitation; it is a class D felony.
acts: engages in vaginal sexual contact with another person
engages in oral sexual contact with another person
engages in anal sexual contact with another person

130.35.plain: Rape in the first degree is vaginal, oral or anal sexual contact by forcible compulsion, with a physically helpless person, with a child under eleven, or under thirteen by an actor eighteen or older; it is a class B felony.
acts: engages in vaginal sexual contact with another person
engages in oral sexual contact with another person
engages in anal sexual contact with another person

130.52.plain: Forcible touching is intentionally and for no legitimate purpose forcibly touching another's intimate parts, or subjecting a transit passenger to sexual contact, for a prohibited purpose; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: forcibly touches the sexual or other intimate parts of another person
subjects another person to sexual contact

130.53.plain: Persistent sexual abuse is committing forcible touching or sexual abuse in the second or third degree after two or more prior qualifying convictions within ten years; it is a class E felony.
acts: commits the crime of forcible touching, as defined in section 130.52 of this article, sexual abuse in the third degree, as defined in section 130.55 of this article, or sexual abuse in the second degree, as defined in section 130.60 of this article

130.55.plain: Sexual abuse in the third degree is subjecting another person to sexual contact without consent; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: subjects another person to sexual contact without the latter's consent

130.60.plain: Sexual abuse in the second degree is subjecting to sexual contact a person incapable of consent for a reason other than being under seventeen, or under fourteen; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: subjects another person to sexual contact

130.65.plain: Sexual abuse in the first degree is subjecting another person to sexual contact by force, or when the person is physically helpless or very young; it is a class D felony.
acts: subjects another person to sexual contact

130.65-A.plain: Aggravated sexual abuse in the fourth degree is inserting a foreign object, or a finger causing injury, into a person incapable of consent for a reason other than being under seventeen; it is a class E felony.
acts: inserts a foreign object in the vagina, urethra, penis, rectum or anus of another person
inserts a finger in the vagina, urethra, penis, rectum or anus of another person causing physical injury to such person

130.66.plain: Aggravated sexual abuse in the third degree is inserting a foreign object or finger into another person by force, or when helpless or very young, or causing injury to a mentally incapable person; class D felony.
acts: inserts a foreign object or a finger in the vagina, urethra, penis, rectum or anus of another person
inserts a foreign object in the vagina, urethra, penis, rectum or anus of another person causing physical injury to such person

130.67.plain: Aggravated sexual abuse in the second degree is inserting a finger into another person causing physical injury, by force or when helpless or under eleven; it is a class C felony.
acts: inserts a finger in the vagina, urethra, penis, rectum or anus of another person causing physical injury to such person

130.70.plain: Aggravated sexual abuse in the first degree is inserting a foreign object into another person causing physical injury, by force or when helpless or under eleven; it is a class B felony.
acts: inserts a foreign object in the vagina, urethra, penis, rectum or anus of another person causing physical injury to such person

130.75.plain: Course of sexual conduct against a child in the first degree is two or more acts of sexual conduct over at least three months with a young child; it is a class B felony.
acts: engages in two or more acts of sexual conduct, which includes at least one act of vaginal sexual contact, oral sexual contact, anal sexual contact or aggravated sexual contact, with a child less than eleven years old

engages in two or more acts of sexual conduct, which include at least one act of vaginal sexual contact, oral sexual contact, anal sexual contact or aggravated sexual contact, with a child less than thirteen years old

130.80.plain: Course of sexual conduct against a child in the second degree is two or more acts of sexual conduct over at least three months with a young child; it is a class D felony.
acts: engages in two or more acts of sexual conduct with a child less than eleven years old
engages in two or more acts of sexual conduct with a child less than thirteen years old

130.85.plain: Female genital mutilation is knowingly cutting a person under eighteen's genitals, or a responsible adult knowingly consenting to it; it is a class E felony.
acts: circumcises, excises, or infibulates the whole or any part of the labia majora or labia minora or clitoris of another person who has not reached eighteen years of age
consents to the circumcision, excision or infibulation of whole or part of such child's labia majora or labia minora or clitoris

130.90.plain: Facilitating a sex offense with a controlled substance is administering a controlled substance or prescription substance without consent to commit a felony of this article, then committing or attempting it; class D felony.
acts: possesses a controlled substance or any preparation, compound, mixture or substance that requires a prescription to obtain and administers such substance or preparation, compound, mixture or substance that requires a prescription to obtain to another person without such person's consent
commits or attempts to commit such conduct constituting a felony defined in this article

130.91.plain: A sexually motivated felony is committing a specified offense for the purpose, in whole or substantial part, of one's own direct sexual gratification; this section states no class.
acts: commits a specified offense

130.92.plain: Sets sentencing consequences for a sexually motivated felony: it may be deemed a violent felony offense, takes the offense level of the specified offense, and is sentenced under section 70.80.

130.95.plain: Predatory sexual assault is committing first degree rape, aggravated sexual abuse or course of sexual conduct against a child with listed aggravating facts; it is a class A-II felony.
acts: commits the crime of rape in the first degree, a crime formerly defined in section 130.50 of this title, the crime of aggravated sexual abuse in the first degree, or course of sexual conduct against a child in the first degree, as defined in this article

130.96.plain: Predatory sexual assault against a child is, by a person eighteen or older, first degree rape, aggravated sexual abuse or course of sexual conduct against a child with a victim under thirteen; class A-II felony.
acts: commits the crime of rape in the first degree, a crime formerly defined in section 130.50 of this title, the crime of aggravated sexual abuse in the first degree, or course of sexual conduct against a child in the first degree, as defined in this article

135.00.plain: Defines restrain, abduct and relative for the kidnapping and unlawful imprisonment article.

135.05.plain: Unlawful imprisonment in the second degree is restraining another person; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: restrains another person

135.10.plain: Unlawful imprisonment in the first degree is restraining another person in circumstances that expose that person to a risk of serious physical injury; it is a class E felony.
acts: restrains another person under circumstances which expose the latter to a risk of serious physical injury

135.15.plain: Gives an affirmative defense to unlawful imprisonment where the defendant was a relative of a child under sixteen whose sole purpose was to assume control of the child.

135.20.plain: Kidnapping in the second degree is abducting another person; it is a class B felony.
acts: abducts another person

135.25.plain: Kidnapping in the first degree is abducting a person with ransom or similar intent, restraining over twelve hours with listed intent, or where the person abducted dies; it is a class A-I felony.
acts: abducts another person

135.30.plain: Gives an affirmative defense to kidnapping where the defendant was a relative of the person abducted and his sole purpose was to assume control of that person.

135.35.plain: Labor trafficking is compelling or inducing another to engage in labor, or recruiting, enticing, harboring or transporting a person, by listed coercive means; it is a class D felony.
acts: compels or induces another to engage in labor or recruits, entices, harbors, or transports such other person

135.36.plain: Provides that a person compelled, induced, recruited, enticed, harbored or transported to engage in labor is not deemed an accomplice in a labor trafficking prosecution.

135.37.plain: Aggravated labor trafficking is compelling or inducing labor, or recruiting or transporting a person for labor, by unlawfully providing a controlled substance to impair judgment; it is a class C felony.
acts: compels or induces another to engage in labor or recruits, entices, harbors, or transports such other person to engage in labor

135.45.plain: Custodial interference in the second degree is a relative taking or enticing a child under sixteen, or anyone taking or enticing an incompetent person from lawful custody; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: takes or entices such child from his lawful custodian
takes or entices from lawful custody any incompetent person or other person entrusted by authority of law to the custody of another person or institution

135.50.plain: Custodial interference in the first degree is custodial interference in the second degree while removing the victim from the state or endangering the victim's safety or health; it is a class E felony.
acts: commits the crime of custodial interference in the second degree
he removes such person from the state

135.55.plain: Substitution of children is, having been entrusted with a child under one year old, substituting, producing or returning a different child to the parent or custodian intending to deceive; it is a class E felony.
acts: substitutes, produces or returns to such parent, guardian or custodian a child other than the one entrusted

135.60.plain: Coercion in the third degree is compelling or inducing a person to do or not do something they have a legal right to, by instilling fear of listed harms; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: compels or induces a person to engage in conduct which the latter has a legal right to abstain from engaging in
to abstain from engaging in conduct in which he or she has a legal right to engage
compels or induces a person to join a group, organization or criminal enterprise which such latter person has a right to abstain from joining
compels or induces a person to produce, disseminate, or otherwise display an image or images depicting nudity of such person or depicting such person engaged in sexual conduct

135.61.plain: Coercion in the second degree is committing coercion in the third degree and thereby compelling or inducing a person to engage in vaginal, oral or anal sexual contact; it is a class E felony.
acts: compels or induces a person to engage in vaginal sexual contact, oral sexual contact or anal sexual contact

135.65.plain: Coercion in the first degree is committing coercion in the third degree by instilling fear of injury or property damage, or by compelling the victim to commit a felony, cause injury, or violate public duty; it is a class D felony.
acts: commits such crime by instilling in the victim a fear that he or she will cause physical injury to a person or cause damage to property
compels or induces the victim to

135.70.plain: Coercion and certain bribe receiving crimes are not mutually exclusive, and committing one of those bribe receiving crimes by the same conduct is no defense to a coercion prosecution.

135.75.plain: Sets an affirmative defense to coercion by threat of criminal charges where the defendant reasonably believed the charge true and sought only reasonable action to make good the wrong.

140.00.plain: Defines premises, building, dwelling, night, and entering or remaining unlawfully for the burglary and trespass article.

140.05.plain: Trespass is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in or upon premises; it is a violation.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in or upon premises

140.10.plain: Criminal trespass in the third degree is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in fenced property, schools, camps, public housing or posted railroad zones under listed circumstances; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a building or upon real property

140.15.plain: Criminal trespass in the second degree is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in a dwelling, or a level two or three registered sex offender entering the school their victim attends or attended; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: nters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling
enters or remains in a public or private elementary, parochial, intermediate, junior high, vocational or high school

140.17.plain: Criminal trespass in the first degree is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in a building while possessing, or knowing a participant possesses, an explosive, deadly weapon, or loaded-capable firearm; it is a class D felony.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a building
Possesses, or knows that another participant in the crime possesses, an explosive or a deadly weapon

Possesses a firearm, rifle or shotgun, as those terms are defined in section 265.00, and also possesses or has readily accessible a quantity of ammunition which is capable of being discharged from such firearm, rifle or shotgun

140.20.plain: Burglary in the third degree is knowingly entering or remaining unlawfully in a building with intent to commit a crime there; it is a class D felony.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a building

140.25.plain: Burglary in the second degree is burglary of a building while armed, injuring someone, using or threatening a dangerous instrument, or displaying an apparent firearm, or burglary of a dwelling; it is a class C felony.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a building

140.30.plain: Burglary in the first degree is burglary of a dwelling while armed, injuring a non-participant, using or threatening a dangerous instrument, or displaying an apparent firearm; it is a class B felony.
acts: enters or remains unlawfully in a dwelling

140.35.plain: Possession of burglar's tools is possessing tools adapted, designed or commonly used for forcible entry, larceny by physical taking, or certain theft of services, intending or knowing they will be so used; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: possesses any tool, instrument or other article adapted, designed or commonly used for committing or facilitating offenses involving forcible entry into premises, or offenses involving larceny by a physical taking, or offenses involving theft of services as defined in subdivisions four, five and six of section 165.15

140.40.plain: Unlawful possession of a radio device is possessing a police-frequency or two-way radio device intending to use it in robbery, burglary, larceny, gambling or an Article 220 violation; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: possesses a radio device

145.00.plain: Criminal mischief in the fourth degree covers intentionally damaging another's property, destroying an abandoned building, recklessly damaging property over $250, or disabling emergency communication equipment; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: damages property of another person
participates in the destruction of an abandoned building as defined in section one thousand nine hundred seventy-one-a of the real property actions and proceedings law
damages property of another person in an amount exceeding two hundred fifty dollars
disables or removes telephonic, TTY or similar communication sending equipment

145.05.plain: Criminal mischief in the third degree is intentionally damaging another's property over $250, or breaking into a locked vehicle to steal after three prior criminal mischief convictions in ten years; it is a class E felony.
acts: damages the motor vehicle of another person, by breaking into such vehicle when it is locked
damages property of another person in an amount exceeding two hundred fifty dollars

145.10.plain: Criminal mischief in the second degree is intentionally damaging another person's property in an amount over $1,500 without right; it is a class D felony.
acts: damages property of another person in an amount exceeding one thousand five hundred dollars

145.12.plain: Criminal mischief in the first degree is intentionally damaging another person's property by means of an explosive without right; it is a class B felony.
acts: damages property of another person by means of an explosive

145.13.plain: Defines "property of another" for the criminal mischief sections to include any property in which another person has an ownership interest, even if the person damaging it also has one.

145.14.plain: Criminal tampering in the third degree is tampering with another person's property without right, intending to cause substantial inconvenience; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: tampers with property of another person

145.15.plain: Criminal tampering in the second degree is tampering or making connection with utility, carrier or power-plant property without right; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: tampers or makes connection with property of a gas, electric, sewer, steam or water-works corporation, telephone or telegraph corporation, common carrier, nuclear powered electric generating facility, or public utility operated by a municipality or district

145.20.plain: Criminal tampering in the first degree is damaging or tampering with utility, carrier or power-plant property to substantially interrupt or impair public service, and causing that interruption; it is a class D felony.
acts: damages or tampers with property of a gas, electric, sewer, steam or water-works corporation, telephone or telegraph corporation, common carrier, nuclear powered electric generating facility, or public utility operated by a municipality or district
causes such substantial interruption or impairment of service

145.22.plain: Cemetery desecration in the second degree is intentionally damaging cemetery or grave property, or stealing personal property located at a grave or burial place; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: damages any real or personal property maintained as a cemetery plot, grave, burial place or other place of interment of human remains
steals personal property which is located at a cemetery plot, grave, burial place or other place of interment of human remains

145.23.plain: Cemetery desecration in the first degree is damaging cemetery property or stealing grave property worth over $250, or repeating second-degree cemetery desecration within five years; it is a class E felony.
acts: damages any real or personal property maintained as a cemetery plot, grave, burial place or other place of interment of human remains in an amount exceeding two hundred fifty dollars
steals personal property, the value of which exceeds two hundred fifty dollars
commits the crime of cemetery desecration in the second degree as defined in section 145.22 of this article

145.25.plain: Reckless endangerment of property is recklessly creating a substantial risk of over $250 in damage to another person's property; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: engages in conduct which creates a substantial risk of damage to the property of another person in an amount exceeding two hundred fifty dollars

145.26.plain: Aggravated cemetery desecration in the second degree is opening an interred casket or crypt and removing remains or objects to obtain unlawful possession of them; it is a class E felony.
acts: opens a casket, crypt, or similar vessel containing a human body or human remains
unlawfully removes therefrom a body, bodily part, any human remains or any object contained in such casket, crypt or similar vessel

145.27.plain: Aggravated cemetery desecration in the first degree is committing aggravated cemetery desecration in the second degree after a cemetery desecration conviction within the past five years; it is a class D felony.
acts: commits the crime of aggravated cemetery desecration in the second degree

145.30.plain: Unlawfully posting advertisements is affixing an advertisement or notice to another's property without right; vendors are presumed to have placed commercial ads; it is a violation.
acts: posts, paints or otherwise affixes to the property of another person any advertisement, poster, notice or other matter designed to benefit a person other than the owner of the property

145.35.plain: Defines "consumer product" for the consumer product tampering sections as any drug, food, beverage or thing offered for sale to the public for ingestion by or application to a human being.

145.40.plain: Tampering with a consumer product in the second degree is contaminating a consumer product intending to injure someone or make them fear injury; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: alters, adulterates or otherwise contaminates a consumer product

145.45.plain: Tampering with a consumer product in the first degree is contaminating a consumer product to injure or frighten and thereby creating a substantial risk of serious physical injury; it is a class E felony.
acts: alters, adulterates or otherwise contaminates a consumer product and thereby creates a substantial risk of serious physical injury to one or more persons

145.50.plain: Bars throwing or dumping refuse, garbage or offensive matter on railroad tracks or rights-of-way, punishable by a fine of up to $250 and/or up to eight hours of service, more for repeats.
acts: throw, dump, or cause to be thrown, dumped, deposited or placed upon any railroad tracks, or within the limits of the rights-of-way of any railroad, any refuse, trash, garbage, rubbish, litter or any nauseous or offensive matter

145.60.plain: Making graffiti is marking any building or other property with intent to damage it without the express permission of the owner or operator; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: make graffiti of any type on any building, public or private, or any other property real or personal owned by any person, firm or corporation or any public agency or instrumentality

145.65.plain: Possession of graffiti instruments is possessing tools or substances made or commonly used to mark property, under circumstances showing intent to use them to damage property one has no permission to mark; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: possesses any tool, instrument, article, substance, solution or other compound designed or commonly used to etch, paint, cover, draw upon or otherwise place a mark upon a piece of property which that person has no permission or authority to etch, paint, cover, draw upon or otherwise mark

145.70.plain: Criminal possession of a taximeter accelerating device is knowingly possessing a device that makes a taxi meter charge more than local law permits, intending to use it unlawfully; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: possesses, with intent to use unlawfully, a taximeter accelerating device

150.00.plain: Defines "building" and "motor vehicle" for the arson article; it creates no crime of its own.

150.01.plain: Arson in the fifth degree is intentionally damaging another's property, without the owner's consent, by intentionally starting a fire or causing an explosion; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: damages property of another without consent of the owner
starting a fire or causing an explosion

150.05.plain: Arson in the fourth degree is recklessly damaging a building or motor vehicle by intentionally starting a fire or causing an explosion; it is a class E felony.
acts: damages a building or motor vehicle
starting a fire or causing an explosion

150.10.plain: Arson in the third degree is intentionally damaging a building or motor vehicle by starting a fire or causing an explosion; it is a class C felony.
acts: damages a building or motor vehicle by starting a fire or causing an explosion

150.15.plain: Arson in the second degree is intentionally damaging a building or motor vehicle by fire when a non-participant is present and the defendant knows or should see that as reasonably possible; it is a class B felony.
acts: damages a building or motor vehicle by starting a fire

150.20.plain: Arson in the first degree is intentionally damaging an occupied building or motor vehicle by explosion or fire using an incendiary device or explosive, causing serious injury, or for profit; it is a class A-I felony.
acts: damages a building or motor vehicle by causing an explosion or a fire

155.00.plain: Defines property, obtain, deprive, appropriate, owner, credit card, service, elderly person and other terms used in the theft title; it creates no crime of its own.

155.05.plain: Defines larceny and the ways it is committed, including by trick, lost property, false promise, extortion, wage theft and deed theft; the crimes and their classes are set in other sections.

155.10.plain: Provides that larceny by extortion and the listed bribe-receiving crimes are not mutually exclusive, so committing bribe receiving is no defense to larceny by extortion.

155.15.plain: Sets affirmative defenses to larceny: a good-faith claim of right for trespassory taking or embezzlement, and a reasonable belief in a threatened charge for certain extortion.

155.20.plain: Sets how the value of stolen property is determined for theft crimes, including market value, written instruments, utilities, and a default of less than two hundred fifty dollars.

155.25.plain: Petit larceny is stealing property; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: steals property

155.30.plain: Grand larceny in the fourth degree is stealing property worth over $1,000 or of listed kinds, such as public records, credit cards, firearms, motor vehicles, or property taken from a person or by extortion; it is a class E felony.
acts: steals property

155.35.plain: Grand larceny in the third degree is stealing property worth over $3,000, an ATM or its contents, retail goods over $3,000 in a common scheme, or deed theft of one commercial property; it is a class D felony.
acts: steals property
commits deed theft of one commercial real property

155.40.plain: Grand larceny in the second degree is stealing property worth over $50,000, obtaining property by certain extortion threats, retail theft over $50,000 in a common scheme, or listed deed thefts; it is a class C felony.
acts: steals property
commits deed theft, regardless of the value, of

155.42.plain: Grand larceny in the first degree is stealing property worth over $1 million, retail theft over $1 million in a common scheme, or deed theft of an occupied home, a vulnerable owner's home, or three or more homes; it is a class B felony.
acts: steals property
commits deed theft, regardless of the value, of

155.43.plain: Aggravated grand larceny of an automated teller machine is stealing an ATM or its contents after a grand larceny third-degree conviction within the previous five years; it is a class C felony.
acts: commits the crime of grand larceny in the third degree

155.45.plain: Sets pleading and proof rules for larceny charges, including when an indictment must specify taking from the person or extortion; it creates no crime of its own.

156.00.plain: Defines computer, computer program, computer data, computer material, access, without authorization and other terms for the computer offenses; it creates no crime of its own.

156.05.plain: Unauthorized use of a computer is knowingly using, causing to be used, or accessing a computer, computer service or network without authorization; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: uses, causes to be used, or accesses a computer, computer service, or computer network without authorization

156.10.plain: Computer trespass is knowingly using or accessing a computer without authorization either to commit or further a felony or thereby knowingly gaining access to computer material; it is a class E felony.
acts: uses, causes to be used, or accesses a computer, computer service, or computer network without authorization
gains access to computer material

156.20.plain: Computer tampering in the fourth degree is using or accessing a computer without authorization and intentionally altering or destroying another person's computer data or program; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: uses, causes to be used, or accesses a computer, computer service, or computer network without authorization
alters in any manner or destroys computer data or a computer program of another person

156.25.plain: Computer tampering in the third degree is fourth-degree computer tampering plus felony intent, a prior conviction, destroying computer material, over $1,000 in damage, or altering COVID-19 vaccination records; it is a class E felony.
acts: commits the crime of computer tampering in the fourth degree
alters in any manner or destroys computer material
alters in any manner or destroys computer data or a computer program so as to cause damages in an aggregate amount exceeding one thousand dollars
enters or alters in any manner or destroys computer material indicating that a person did or did not receive a vaccination against COVID-19

156.26.plain: Computer tampering in the second degree is fourth-degree computer tampering that intentionally causes over $3,000 in damage or alters medical records causing serious physical injury; it is a class D felony.
acts: commits the crime of computer tampering in the fourth degree
alters in any manner or destroys

156.27.plain: Computer tampering in the first degree is fourth-degree computer tampering that intentionally alters or destroys computer data or programs causing over $50,000 in damages; it is a class C felony.
acts: commits the crime of computer tampering in the fourth degree
alters in any manner or destroys computer data or a computer program so as to cause damages in an aggregate amount exceeding fifty thousand dollars

156.29.plain: Unlawful duplication of computer related material in the second degree is copying computer medical records without right, intending to commit or further a crime under this chapter; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: copies, reproduces or duplicates in any manner computer material that contains records of the medical history or medical treatment of an identified or readily identifiable individual or individuals

156.30.plain: Unlawful duplication of computer related material in the first degree is copying computer data or programs without right to wrongfully take over $2,500 in value or to further a felony; it is a class E felony.
acts: copies, reproduces or duplicates in any manner:
deprives or appropriates from an owner thereof an economic value or benefit in excess of two thousand five hundred dollars

156.35.plain: Criminal possession of computer related material is knowingly possessing, without right, an unlawfully duplicated copy of computer data or a program, to benefit oneself or a non-owner; it is a class E felony.
acts: possesses, in any form, any copy, reproduction or duplicate of any computer data or computer program which was copied, reproduced or duplicated in violation of section 156.30 of this article

156.40.plain: Operating an unlawful electronic sweepstakes is knowingly possessing an electronic machine or device, intending to operate it, to conduct or promote a sweepstakes through an entertaining display; it is a class E felony.
acts: conduct a sweepstakes through the use of an entertaining display, including the entry process or the reveal of a prize
promote a sweepstakes that is conducted through the use of an entertaining display, including the entry process or the reveal of a prize

156.50.plain: Sets defenses to computer offenses where the defendant had reasonable grounds to believe he was authorized to use the computer or had the right to alter, destroy or copy the data or program; it creates no crime.

158.00.plain: Defines "public benefit card", "fraudulent welfare act" and "public assistance benefits" for the welfare fraud article, sets a rebuttable presumption for possessing five or more cards, and a limitation; it creates no crime.

158.05.plain: Welfare fraud in the fifth degree is committing a fraudulent welfare act and thereby taking or obtaining public assistance benefits; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: commits a fraudulent welfare act and thereby takes or obtains public assistance benefits

158.10.plain: Welfare fraud in the fourth degree is committing a fraudulent welfare act and thereby taking or obtaining public assistance benefits worth more than one thousand dollars; it is a class E felony.
acts: commits a fraudulent welfare act and thereby takes or obtains public assistance benefits

158.15.plain: Welfare fraud in the third degree is committing a fraudulent welfare act and thereby taking or obtaining public assistance benefits worth more than three thousand dollars; it is a class D felony.
acts: commits a fraudulent welfare act and thereby takes or obtains public assistance benefits

158.20.plain: Welfare fraud in the second degree is committing a fraudulent welfare act and thereby taking or obtaining public assistance benefits worth more than fifty thousand dollars; it is a class C felony.
acts: commits a fraudulent welfare act and thereby takes or obtains public assistance benefits

158.25.plain: Welfare fraud in the first degree is committing a fraudulent welfare act and thereby taking or obtaining public assistance benefits worth more than one million dollars; it is a class B felony.
acts: commits a fraudulent welfare act and thereby takes or obtains public assistance benefits

158.30.plain: Criminal use of a public benefit card in the second degree is knowingly taking a benefit card as loan collateral, obtaining one for a benefit, or transferring one for money, drugs or an unlawful purpose; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: accepts a public benefit card as collateral or security
Obtains a public benefit card in exchange for a benefit
Transfers or delivers a public benefit card to another

158.35.plain: Criminal use of a public benefit card in the first degree is knowingly obtaining three or more benefit cards for a benefit, or transferring three or more for money or a controlled substance; it is a class E felony.
acts: obtains three or more public benefit cards from another or others in exchange for a benefit
transfers or delivers three or more public benefit cards to another or others

158.40.plain: Criminal possession of public benefit cards in the third degree is knowingly possessing five or more benefit cards in other people's names, with intent to defraud, deceive or injure another; it is a class E felony.
acts: possesses five or more public benefit cards in a name or names other than the person's own name

158.45.plain: Criminal possession of public benefit cards in the second degree is knowingly possessing ten or more benefit cards in other people's names, with intent to defraud, deceive or injure another; it is a class D felony.
acts: possesses ten or more public benefit cards in a name or names other than the person's own name

158.50.plain: Criminal possession of public benefit cards in the first degree is knowingly possessing twenty-five or more benefit cards in other people's names, with intent to defraud, deceive or injure another; it is a class C felony.
acts: possesses twenty-five or more public benefit cards in a name or names other than the person's own name

160.00.plain: Defines robbery as forcible stealing: using or threatening immediate physical force during a larceny to overcome resistance or compel delivery of property; it sets no class and creates no separate crime.

160.05.plain: Robbery in the third degree is forcibly stealing property; it is a class D felony.
acts: forcibly steals property

160.10.plain: Robbery in the second degree is forcibly stealing property while aided by someone present, while injuring a non-participant or displaying an apparent firearm, or when the property is a motor vehicle; it is a class C felony.
acts: forcibly steals property
Causes physical injury to any person who is not a participant in the crime
Displays what appears to be a pistol, revolver, rifle, shotgun, machine gun or other firearm

160.15.plain: Robbery in the first degree is forcibly stealing property while seriously injuring a non-participant, being armed with a deadly weapon, using or threatening a dangerous instrument, or displaying an apparent firearm; it is a class B felony.
acts: forcibly steals property
Causes serious physical injury to any person who is not a participant in the crime
Is armed with a deadly weapon
Uses or threatens the immediate use of a dangerous instrument
Displays what appears to be a pistol, revolver, rifle, shotgun, machine gun or other firearm

165.00.plain: Misapplication of property is, while knowingly holding another's property under a return agreement, encumbering it without consent so the owner risks loss, or intentionally refusing to return rented property after written demand; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: loans, leases, pledges, pawns or otherwise encumbers such property
refuses to return personal property valued in excess of one hundred dollars to the owner

165.05.plain: Unauthorized use of a vehicle in the third degree is knowingly using a vehicle without the owner's consent, or intentionally misusing or overkeeping a vehicle held under a service or return agreement; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: takes, operates, exercises control over, rides in or otherwise uses a vehicle
uses or operates the same
retains or withholds possession thereof

165.06.plain: Unauthorized use of a vehicle in the second degree is committing third-degree unauthorized use under subdivision one of section 165.05 after a prior such conviction within ten years; it is a class E felony.
acts: commits the crime of unauthorized use of a vehicle in the third degree as defined in subdivision one of section 165.05 of this article

165.07.plain: Unlawful use of secret scientific material is, without right, making a copy or record of secret scientific material, intending to appropriate its use; it is a class E felony.
acts: makes a tangible reproduction or representation of such secret scientific material

165.08.plain: Unauthorized use of a vehicle in the first degree is knowingly using a vehicle without the owner's consent, intending to use it in committing or fleeing a class A, B, C or D felony; it is a class D felony.
acts: takes, operates, exercises control over, rides in or otherwise uses a vehicle

165.09.plain: Auto stripping in the third degree is removing, or intentionally destroying or defacing, any part of a vehicle without the owner's permission, or of an abandoned vehicle without authority; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: removes
destroys or defaces any part of a vehicle
destroys or defaces any part of an abandoned vehicle

165.10.plain: Auto stripping in the second degree is third-degree auto stripping after a prior conviction within five years, or stripping parts worth over one thousand dollars from two or more vehicles without permission; it is a class E felony.
acts: commits the offense of auto stripping in the third degree
removes
destroys, defaces, disguises, or alters any part of two or more vehicles

165.11.plain: Auto stripping in the first degree is removing, or intentionally destroying, defacing, disguising or altering, parts of three or more vehicles without permission, worth over three thousand dollars in all; it is a class D felony.
acts: removes
destroys, defaces, disguises, or alters any part of three or more vehicles

165.15.plain: Theft of services covers obtaining or avoiding payment for services such as restaurants, hotels, transit, telecommunications, utilities, admissions, labor, computers and salons by fraud, stealth or tampering; it is a class A misdemeanor, some first offenses are violations, and some telephone theft is a class E felony.
acts: obtains or attempts to obtain a service, or induces or attempts to induce the supplier of a rendered service to agree to payment therefor on a credit basis
avoids or attempts to avoid such payment
obtains or attempts to obtain such service or avoids or attempts to avoid payment therefor
obtains or attempts to obtain such service for himself or another person or avoids or attempts to avoid payment therefor by himself or another person
sells, offers for sale or otherwise makes available, without consent, an existing, canceled or revoked access device
uses, without consent, an existing, canceled or revoked access device
obtains any telecommunications service
tampers with such device or with other equipment related thereto
accepts or receives the use and benefit of service
tampers with any equipment designed to supply or to prevent the supply of such service
obtains or attempts to obtain such admission without payment of the lawful charge therefor
uses or diverts to the use of himself or a third person such labor, equipment or facilities
uses, causes to be used, accesses, or attempts to use or access a computer, computer service, or computer network and avoids or attempts to avoid payment therefor

165.16.plain: Unauthorized sale of certain transportation services is selling, without authorization, access to MTA or New York city transit service with an unlimited or doctored farecard in a transit facility; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: sells access to such transportation services to such person

165.17.plain: Unlawful use of a credit card, debit card or public benefit card is using or displaying a card one knows is revoked or cancelled to obtain property or a service; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: uses or displays a credit card, debit card or public benefit card

165.20.plain: Fraudulently obtaining a signature is getting someone to sign a written instrument through a known false misrepresentation, intending to defraud or injure or to gain a substantial benefit; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: obtains the signature of a person to a written instrument

165.25.plain: Jostling is, in a public place, intentionally and unnecessarily putting a hand near someone's pocket or handbag, or jostling a person while another's hand is near their pocket or handbag; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: Places his hand in the proximity of a person's pocket or handbag
Jostles or crowds another person

165.30.plain: Fraudulent accosting is accosting a person in a public place intending to defraud him of money or property by a trick, swindle or confidence game; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: accosts a person in a public place

165.35.plain: Fortune telling is claiming or pretending to tell fortunes, or claiming occult powers to answer questions, give advice or affect evil spirits or curses, for a fee; it is a class B misdemeanor.
acts: claims or pretends to tell fortunes
holds himself out as being able, by claimed or pretended use of occult powers, to answer questions or give advice on personal matters or to exorcise, influence or affect evil spirits or curses

165.40.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the fifth degree is knowingly possessing stolen property with intent to benefit oneself or another non-owner or to impede recovery by an owner; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: possesses stolen property

165.45.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the fourth degree is knowingly possessing stolen property over $1,000, certain cards, firearms, motor vehicles, religious items or ammonia, or as a dealer; it is a class E felony.
acts: possesses stolen property

165.50.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the third degree is knowingly possessing stolen property worth more than $3,000, with intent to benefit a non-owner or impede recovery; it is a class D felony.
acts: possesses stolen property

165.52.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the second degree is knowingly possessing stolen property worth more than $50,000, with intent to benefit a non-owner or impede recovery; it is a class C felony.
acts: possesses stolen property

165.54.plain: Criminal possession of stolen property in the first degree is knowingly possessing stolen property worth more than $1 million, with intent to benefit a non-owner or impede recovery; it is a class B felony.
acts: possesses stolen property

165.55.plain: Sets presumptions for criminal possession of stolen property: of intent to benefit or impede recovery, and of knowledge that property was stolen for dealers and possessors of multiple stolen cards or air tickets; it creates no crime.

165.60.plain: Says it is no defense to criminal possession of stolen property that the thief was not caught, that the defendant stole the property, or that the larceny occurred outside the state; it creates no crime.

165.65.plain: Sets corroboration rules for convicting a person of criminal possession of stolen property on accomplice testimony or the testimony of those he obtained it from or disposed of it to; it creates no crime.

165.66.plain: Fostering the sale of stolen goods is using a website, platform or location to offer for sale retail goods one knew or should have known were stolen, for financial gain; it is a class A misdemeanor.
acts: Uses any internet website, application, online marketplace, digital service, or any other platform or venue, including any physical building, public or private space, or location to offer for sale retail goods or merchandise which are stolen or unlawfully obtained

165.70.plain: Defines "trademark", "counterfeit trademark", "traffic" and "goods" for the trademark counterfeiting sections 165.71 through 165.74; it creates no crime.

165.71.plain: Trademark counterfeiting in the third degree is making, distributing or selling goods bearing a counterfeit trademark, or possessing a counterfeit trademark to affix to goods, to deceive or defraud; it is a class a misdemeanor.
acts: manufactures, distributes, sells, or offers for sale goods which bear a counterfeit trademark
possesses a trademark

165.72.plain: Trademark counterfeiting in the second degree is making, distributing or selling goods bearing a counterfeit trademark, or possessing a counterfeit trademark to affix to goods, to deceive or defraud with retail value over $1,000; it is a class e felony.
acts: manufactures, distributes, sells, or offers for sale goods which bear a counterfeit trademark
possesses a trademark

165.73.plain: Trademark counterfeiting in the first degree is making, distributing or selling goods bearing a counterfeit trademark, or possessing a counterfeit trademark to affix to goods, to deceive or defraud with retail value over $100,000; it is a class c felony.
acts: manufactures, distributes, sells, or offers for sale goods which bear a counterfeit trademark
possesses a trademark

165.74.plain: Allows police to seize goods bearing counterfeit trademarks, requires a probable-cause hearing within forty-eight hours of arraignment, and directs destruction or donation of the goods on conviction; it creates no crime.
